title.narrative: Service Level Agreement with the General Secretariat of the Council for the organisation of the International Conference on Supporting the future of Syria and the Region (Brussels VII Conference) On 15 June 2023

description.narrative:
Service Level Agreement with the General Secretariat of the Council for the organisation of the International Conference on ¿Supporting the future of Syria and the Region¿ (Brussels VII Conference) On 15 June 2023


The organisation of this conference is of the highest political importance involving the participation of high-level political representatives, including Heads of State and Government, 2 Commissioners and the HRVP. Traditionally, previous editions of the Brussels Conference for Syria and the future of its region have been hosted by the Council and organised in the Europa building (used by of the Council of Ministers of the EU). The Council will provide for the necessary logistical and secure connection arrangements, needed for the organisation of this online global conference. As such, the Council has the required resources in terms of technical knowhow and manpower to ensure the smooth running of this high-level event.

The Council has the ideal venue for the Ministerial event as it is the only building capable of accommodating the number of representatives who will be invited, including the necessary protocol services and necessary security requirements. In addition, the Brussels Conferences have been historically linked to the Council building, the public website of the Brussels Conference is embedded to the Council¿s website and it acts as a reference site. It has the repository of all published documents, which is essential in an era where digital communication is a key element of success for the right narrative to be shared globally. Having the possibility of using such a reference site is an invaluable asset.

The Council of Ministers has exclusive rights on this building and the General Secretariat of the Council (GSC) is the only possible contracting counterpart. It is therefore necessary to use the SLA contract foreseen by both institutions rather than a standard service contract. The sums mentioned in the SLA are lower than last year¿s SLA and were provided by Council services according to their estimates, established during consultations with EEAS.

There is a clear provision in the SLA Art. 3(2) that the Council will pay back all the unused amounts as was always the case in the past. The final invoicing shall be done on the basis of actual costs.
